LESSON: DANGERS OF HEAT

Grade: Grade 3
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: Environment 1.6 Energy: Heat By the end of the sub-strand, the  Using relevant 
Topic 1.6.3: Dangers of heat

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Dangers of heat. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify materials that can start fire in the house
2. identify dangers of heat energy at home
3. demonstrate an understanding of safe ways of moving from the house in case of a fire outbreak. more information on fires and safety procedures. “Don’ts “list during fire outbreaks. The list should be shared at school and at home. Core-competence to be development: Collaboration and communication, learning to learn; critical thinking and problem solving. Links to PCI’s: ESD: Disaster Risk Reduction; Environmental Education: Environment and Links to values: Cooperation, responsibility and respect its resources: Energy Life skills: Effective communication; learners discuss in groups dangers of heat at home. Links to other learning activity areas (s): Hygiene and Nutrition fire station

1. identify materials that can start fire in the house

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At school, pick litter and put it in the bin. That cares for the environment.

Example 2: Wash your hands with soap before eating and after using the toilet.

Example 3: Name two foods you eat at home that help you grow strong.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Dangers of heat.
2. Explain Dangers of heat to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Dangers of heat.
4. Show that you can: identify materials that can start fire in the house
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Dangers of heat. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is Dangers of heat important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.
